paragraphs: He is mentioned in Yevamot 60b; Hyman infers from the passage that he lived in Rav Ashi’s time and suggests that the reading should be Rav Huna son of Rav Natan.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Rav Ashi’s explanation in the saved William Davidson Yevamot 60b passage gives context for Hyman’s chronological inference; it does not itself prove a direct exchange or the proposed replacement of Kahana with Huna son of Rav Natan.

The whole Davidson Yevamot 60b paragraph fully names Rav Kahana son of Rav Natan and later Rav Ashi. These support the local full titles, while Hyman’s chronological inference and ‘it seems that the reading should be’ Huna remain his judgments. The proposed father’s name follows the context of Hyman’s heading; neither a direct exchange nor a new teacher or chronology relationship follows.
